verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions run on every incoming event before delivery. They can filter, transform and enrich events, and they can call third-party services over HTTP via the Fetch API, so code-defined logic can trigger actions automatically per event. A webhook destination can also forward events to any HTTP endpoint, and built-in alerts fire on sync or batch failures. However, these 'rules' are JavaScript/TypeScript code inside a data-processing pipeline rather than a documented rule or trigger-action automation feature. missing for 10: declarative rule/trigger-action builder, documented conditional event-to-action automation beyond in-pipeline processing, independent or hands-on corroboration of event-triggered actions

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Functions are designed to process data in Jitsu before it is sent to the destination... Filter... Transform... Enrich
Fetch API - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services.
Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria.
Send data to any HTTP endpoint.
you’ll receive real-time Email or Slack alerts whenever a Connector Sync task or Data Warehouse Batch job fails or successfully recovers
